correctness.rationale: The complete type recursion and characteristic formulas are derived explicitly. A section of the truncation map lets nonroot nodes realize every abstract previous-depth label, while one designated row realizes any requested depth-d type; an induction on semantic depth proves this for arbitrary k and d. The conjunction of all successor-type characteristic formulas forces \(h_{d-1}\) distinct worlds and is realized at this size. The packaged independent checker compares calculated semantic labels against declared types for 66142 exhaustive and 200 sampled cases; finite checks are not substituted for the symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: Lück (arXiv:1709.05253), Section 4, already establishes the exact number of rank-d types and a single universal depth-d canonical model, but does not state the rank-(d-1)-sized model for each individual target type or its sharpness. These nearby results substantially limit the novelty scope to the per-type size optimization. Existing shallow model results give formula-size-dependent bounds (Schroeder–Pattinson 2007/2009), while standard Hintikka formulas give finite rank types (Anttila–Haeggblom–Yang 2025). The accessible 2026 small-frame study reports finite-corpus computations and does not state a sharp uniform cutoff as a function solely of depth and letters. The new claim proves both the cyclic construction on exactly one node per predecessor type and an optimal lower bound for every depth; no inspected claim entails this equality. Priority is qualified by uninspected specialist literature and inaccessible full text of the recent source.
